tagline: Thirty miles of ferry, then the island roads.
intro: The byway starts on the water. The ferry out of Anacortes threads about 30 miles of marine highway through the islands, past Lopez, which is on the route but not on the byway, to Friday Harbor on San Juan Island. From there the roads run out to Roche Harbor on the northwest shore, facing Haro Strait and Canada, and around the island's west side.

A second boat carries on to Orcas Island, for Eastsound and Moran State Park and the road to Olga. On the shore at Lime Kiln Point, back on San Juan, whales can come within 20 feet of the people watching them from shore.

moments.title: San Juan Island National Historical Park
moments.text: In 1859 an American killed a stray British pig, and the two nations kept rival camps on the island until 1872, when the German Kaiser, as arbiter, gave the islands to the United States.

moments.title: Roche Harbor
moments.text: Lime from the company kilns here went along the coast, some of it to San Francisco after the 1906 earthquake, before the town was made over as a boating resort.

moments.title: Moran State Park
moments.text: In 1935 CCC crews began a stone tower atop 2,407-foot Mount Constitution, the highest point in the islands, in a park that was once shipbuilder Robert Moran's estate.

practical: Vehicle reservations on the Washington State Ferries are highly recommended, and sailings are less frequent outside the summer season.
